clue.text: Two animals – requirement for four or six, perhaps?

definitions.text: requirement for four or six, perhaps?

blocks.note: the first animal: a chirping insect
the second animal: a flying mammal

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which pair of creatures a batsman needs to score boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a four or a six is a boundary hit, and you cannot score one without the willow in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the ball to the boundary for four or six runs requires the wooden implement the batsman swings.

clue.text: Everything forgotten by diva with first of high notes, perhaps?

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the named word drops out of the singer's name
only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: Maria Callas, the celebrated opera diva
everything is all
the opening letter of high

explanation.surface: A soprano loses her place but still hits the top notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas was the great Greek-American soprano. 'Notes' looks musical after 'diva' and 'high', but it means banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are an example of money in hand, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Where customs officers may search, whatever happens

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: inside any suitcase at all
second meaning: an idiom for regardless

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition takes the phrase literally, a case being a piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of circumstances, while literally a customs check may look inside any piece of luggage.

clue.text: Greek letter, a couple of pages in the spirit of an Egyptian

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the spirit's name

blocks.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double
taken as written
p is the abbreviation for page, doubled for two

explanation.surface: Odd scene of a Greek character and two leaves of paper inside an ancient soul.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Egyptian belief the ka was one of the parts of the soul, a favourite crossword spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth character of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to K.

clue.text: Butcher I meet at 4pm perhaps?

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the following letters are chopped up and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arranges to meet the local butcher at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a person you would meet; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Four in the afternoon is the traditional British hour for the light meal with tea, so it exemplifies it.

clue.text: Close door at the end, blocking various aisles

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word before is wanted
various suggests differing versions, so the following letters are rearranged
something blocking a passage stands inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the last letter of door

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a door at the end of a theatre's passageways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb ordering the door shut; it is the adjective meaning stuffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather or a close room is stuffy and oppressive, lacking fresh ventilation.

clue.text: Cheerless poet in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means reading the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A gloomy writer looks back on life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and dreary is cheerless, lacking colour or brightness.

clue.text: Jack beams when speaking?

indicators.note: when speaking means we only hear the word, so its sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack smiles broadly while he talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name and 'beams' like smiling; jack up means lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack a car is to lift it with a jack, so jack is a synonym for elevate.

clue.text: Generous sack filled with rubbish I gather

indicators.note: rubbish is worthless and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled
a container filled with something holds it inside

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind person's bag turns out to be stuffed with junk, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag being filled; it is bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A big-hearted person is kind and giving, a synonym for generous.

clue.text: Cold-blooded killer I call ambitious!

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake, literally cold-blooded
taken as written
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A ruthless murderer announces an aim to rise in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded killer' suggests a ruthless person, but a reptile's blood is literally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aspiring hopes to rise to a goal, a synonym for ambitious.

clue.text: Singular instrument needing strings slackened?

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A unique stringed instrument needs its strings loosened.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a string tuned too high must be loosened to bring the pitch down.
explanation.definitionFit: A note above true pitch is sharp, and a string producing it needs loosening to lower it.

clue.text: Lovely job of a police officer

blocks.note: first meaning: striking, eye-catching
second meaning: taking suspects into custody

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pleasant police job; the word is both an adjective and a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking appearance stops you in your tracks, while police detain suspects as their work.

clue.text: Marvellous thing, might one be blown away by it?

definitions.text: might one be blown away by it?

blocks.note: first meaning: informal praise for something sensational

blocks.clueFragment: might one be blown away by it?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: an explosive that blasts things apart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown away' usually means deeply impressed, which echoes the first sense; read literally it is the result of an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive is informally used for anything sensational, and an explosion literally blasts things away.

clue.text: Girl – Frenchman going after one

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman chases after a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' places the Frenchman after the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's first name, and crosswords use girl for any female name.

clue.text: Merchandise as yet not shifting

blocks.note: a shop's goods are its stock
still means up to now

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper complains that goods are still not selling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not shifting' sounds like unsold goods, but means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely motionless is the idiom's meaning, so it fits something not moving at all.

clue.text: Tester of water temperature gulping drink, this food's hot

indicators.note: to gulp is to swallow, so one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: you dip a toe in to test the water
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone testing the bath swigs a drink, then remarks on the hot food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This food's hot' is the definition: a snack served hot from the grill, the wordplay coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a snack served hot.

clue.text: Dancing as sign of being home from beach holiday?

definitions.text: sign of being home from beach holiday?

blocks.note: first meaning: performing a ballroom dance from Argentina

blocks.clueFragment: sign of being home from beach holiday?
blocks.note: second meaning, split into two words: the sun-browned skin fading away once you are back

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker back home shows off a new dance step.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into TAN GOING: a fading suntan shows the holiday is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing the tango, the Argentine ballroom dance, is a form of dancing.

clue.text: Captain, delicate winger?

blocks.note: first meaning: the master of a ship or team leader
second meaning: a small butterfly with a darting flight

explanation.surface: A team captain fields a fragile wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the wing, but here it is something with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a ship's or team's leader and also the name of a family of small butterflies.

clue.text: It, for example, starts to consume everything, say

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: it is an example of a pronoun
the opening letters of consume and everything

explanation.surface: A monster called It devours everything, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a monster or the subject of the sentence; it is a word in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce a word is to utter it, a synonym for say.

clue.text: Make a bundle tilt inside container

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, held within it

blocks.note: a cup is a container
to tilt is to lean

explanation.surface: Instructions for tipping a pile of things into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a bundle' looks like tying things together; a bundle is also slang for a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning up is an idiom for making a big profit, and a bundle is a lot of money.

clue.text: One trying to make others happy, suffering relapse

definitions.text: One trying to make others happy

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked out of shape, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kindly soul who always helps others falls ill again.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleaser is a person who tries to please, as in people-pleaser.

clue.text: Miss married to small man from Italy

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to miss something is to ignore it

explanation.surface: A young lady weds a short Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like an unmarried woman, which 'married' plays on; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Signore is the Italian title for a gentleman, like Mr or sir.

clue.text: Following drive, a companion leaves

blocks.note: a drive in a car is a spin
taken as written
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: After a car trip, a friend goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing; it is a plural noun for foliage you eat. 'Following' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, eaten as its leaves.

clue.text: Salute remedy after cutting oxygen

indicators.note: cutting trims a word, so its last letter is lost

blocks.note: a salve is a healing ointment
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A medical cure is welcomed after a surgeon cuts off the air supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the last letter from SALVE, then add O.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous firing of guns, often as a ceremonial salute.

clue.text: Loaded gun once raised, media mogul backs up

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of each preceding word is kept
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom of the column to the top

blocks.note: the final letters of gun, once, raised, media and mogul

explanation.surface: A press baron's old weapon is lifted, primed and ready, as he retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun', 'raised' and 'media mogul' look like things to translate, but they are only there for their last letters. 'Raised' tempts as the reversal signal, and 'up' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means weighed down with a load, the old past participle of lade, so it is a synonym for loaded.

clue.text: Issue certificate, finally leading to job

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of certificate
a mission is an assigned job

explanation.surface: Getting a qualification eventually leads to employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue certificate' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something given out or discharged, as is an issue.

clue.text: Old German instrument working

blocks.note: short for saxophone
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An elderly German musician plays his instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxons were an ancient Germanic people, some of whom settled in England.

clue.text: Burden lies with you and me?

blocks.note: a duty that lies with someone rests on them
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A shared load falls on both of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads straight through: a burden that rests with you and me is on us.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the burden or duty of responsibility.

clue.text: Country houses one's making somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as a country
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A nation builds homes for its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like the definition, but it is only the outer piece; the definition is 'somewhere in Asia'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Part of oven on, extra switches for gas

indicators.note: part of a run of words means the letters sit within them, spanning the word breaks
switches suggests turning around, so the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of oven, all of on, and the start of extra

explanation.surface: A cook switches the oven on and adds more gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switches' sounds like turning the oven on, and 'extra' like more fuel; the answer is hidden backwards in the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble element, an inert gas used in bright lamps.

clue.text: Family business

blocks.note: first meaning: lineage or descent
second meaning: one's trade or occupation

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a family firm, but the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A family line is a lineage, and one's line of work is one's trade.

clue.text: A shift in roles leaving only odd characters in high spirits

indicators.note: keeping only the odd-numbered characters means taking the first, third and fifth letters
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first, third and fifth letters of roles
a shift is a change

explanation.surface: A change of job leaves only eccentrics in a jolly mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High spirits' looks like cheerfulness, but means exalted spiritual beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangels are angels of the highest rank, so spirits in a lofty position.
